chunks: The Shaykh Abu Ja'far narrated to me by reading to him. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar and Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah narrated to us together, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Yaqtin, from his brother al-Husayn, from his father 'Ali ibn Yaqtin, who said:

Al-Rashid summoned a man to invalidate the authority of Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both) and to refute him and embarrass him in the assembly. So a sorcerer volunteered. When the banquet was brought, he cast a spell upon the bread; whenever the servant of Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) tried to take a loaf, it flew from his hands. Joy and laughter overtook Harun. Then Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) raised his head toward a lion painted on a curtain and said: O lion of Allah, seize the enemy of Allah!

He said: That image leaped forth like the mightiest beast of prey and devoured the sorcerer. Harun and his courtiers fell unconscious, and their minds were blown away in fear. When they recovered after a while, Harun said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): I ask you by my right over you, would you not ask the image to return the man?

So he said: If the staff of Musa (peace be upon him) could return what it swallowed of the people's ropes and staffs, then this image would return what it swallowed of this man. And that was the most effective of things in the awakening of his soul.

key_terms.افترست: Devoured, mauled by a beast of prey
key_terms.عصا موسى: The staff of Musa (Moses), referencing the Quranic miracle (7:117, 20:69)
key_terms.معزم: Sorcerer, conjurer who practices incantation-based magic
key_terms.ناموس: Namus, a magical device or spirit invocation used to control objects

ai.seo_question: What miracle did Imam Musa al-Kadhim perform against the sorcerer at Harun al-Rashid's court?
ai.summary: This narrative recounts a miraculous event at the court of Harun al-Rashid, reported by 'Ali ibn Yaqtin who served as an Abbasid official. Al-Rashid brought a sorcerer to humiliate Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS), but the Imam commanded a painted lion on a curtain to come alive and devour the sorcerer. When Harun begged the Imam to reverse it, the Imam drew a parallel with the Quranic account of Prophet Musa's staff swallowing the sorcerers' ropes (7:117), demonstrating that divine miracles are irreversible.

en.bilal-muhammad: Abu Ja`far narrated to me. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (ra) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Saffar and Sa`d b. `Abdullah narrated together to us from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. `Isa from al-Hasan b. `Ali b. Yaqtin from his father al-Husayn from his father `Ali b. Yaqtin.

He said: [The Caliph Harun] al-Rashid called for a man to invalidate the authority of Abi’l Hasan Musa b. Ja`far (as), to refute him and to embarrass him in the gathering. So, he appointed a sorcerer. When the banquet was brought, he summoned a spirit (namus) over the bread; every time the servant of Abi’l Hasan (as) took a piece of bread, it would fly out of his hands. By that, Harun was overtaken with joy and laughing. Then, Abu’l Hasan (as) lifted his head to an image of a lion [painted] on a fabric. He said to it: O lion of Allah! Seize the enemy of Allah.

He said: The image of the lion leaped into the mightiest of lions and devoured the sorcerer. Then, Harun and his men fell unconscious to their faces – their minds were blown in fear of what they had seen. When they awoke from that after a while, Harun said to Abi’l Hasan (as): I ask you by my right over you – ask this image to bring the man back.

So, he said: If the staff of Musa (as) could return what it swallowed from the ropes of the people, then this image would return what it swallowed from this man. This was from the most effective of things in the awakening of his soul.
